tools.name: StartDeployWebsite
tools.description:
Creates a website on Wix and puts it live, or replaces the files of one deployed earlier. You write the site's code, or take the files the user brought (HTML/CSS/JS, a static build, a zip, another builder's export), and this returns the guide to create the site and upload them. Updates keep the same site and URL. Works with or without a Wix login (anonymous deploy with a save link), through the Wix MCP alone or from a shell. Call it right away, without asking the user anything first.
When a new site needs Wix business features (a store, bookings or appointments, rentals, events and tickets, a restaurant menu with online orders or reservations, a blog, a portfolio, pricing plans and memberships, donations, Wix Forms, members and login, a CMS, payments), call StartHeadlessBuild instead. When the user brought files and the site needs those features, upload the files here first; the upload's result then points to StartHeadlessBuild to connect them.
Returns the guide; follow it and do the work yourself. Upload with UploadHeadlessWebsiteFiles once the site exists; the drop page is only the fallback.
NOT for: a user who asked for Wix's editor, the Wix Harmony Editor, a template, Wix Studio or the Classic Editor (WixHarmonyEditorBuild, SearchSiteTemplates); a Claude Design bundle URL (import-claude-design-from-url); migrating a live site by URL or CSV exports; adding HTML or code into an existing Wix editor site; uploading images or documents to a site's media (UploadImageToWixSite).

tools.name: WixREADME
tools.description:
# Tool: WixREADME
The context every other Wix tool assumes. Call it first, once per conversation, for any Wix task or question; for another site later in the conversation, call `GetSiteContext` instead of calling this again.
A Wix task includes reading or changing a site's or account's data: products, inventory, carts, checkouts, orders, bookings, services, staff, time slots, rentals, restaurant menus, online orders, reservations, events, tickets, RSVPs, blog posts, CMS collections and items, pricing plans, subscriptions, portfolios, gift cards, coupons, donations, forms, form submissions, contacts, members, loyalty points, groups, reviews, inbox messages, CRM tasks, automations, email campaigns, payments, invoices, SEO, redirects, translations, locations, analytics, media files, site properties, installed apps, and the account's sites and domains (searching whether a domain is available, buying one, and connecting one bought elsewhere).
These requests skip it and go straight to their own tool:
- **Creating a new site.** Skip the docs too. A site is written in code and uploaded: StartDeployWebsite returns the upload guide; StartHeadlessBuild returns the headless guide, for a site that needs Wix business features (a store, bookings or appointments, rentals, events and tickets, a restaurant menu with online orders or reservations, a blog, a portfolio, pricing plans and memberships, donations, Wix Forms, members and login, a CMS, payments). Call one right away, without asking the user anything first: StartHeadlessBuild when the site needs Wix business features, otherwise StartDeployWebsite. WixHarmonyEditorBuild or SearchSiteTemplates only when the user asked for Wix's editor, the Wix Harmony Editor, a template, Wix Studio or the Classic Editor. Never create a site through ManageWixSite, CallWixSiteAPI or ExecuteWixAPI.
- **Suggesting domain names**: call GetSuggestedDomains directly, with the business or site name as the query.
- **Listing, showing or finding their Wix sites**: call ListWixSites directly.
- **Uploading local or attached image files to a Wix site**: call UploadImageToWixSite directly, with no docs, schema or API calls. Do NOT use ExecuteWixAPI, SearchWixAPISpec, or any Media Manager REST API for image uploads.
A question about one of those goes to the same tool ("can you show my sites?" is ListWixSites). Any other Wix question is answered from a Wix skill or the docs, never from memory, and never with a reply that you lack the tools to answer.
It returns, in full:
- **Source of truth**: nothing Wix-specific from memory. Every URL, ID, setting location, product fact, request shape and field name comes from the docs tools, a Wix skill, an earlier tool result in the conversation, or the user.
- **The site**: the account's sites with their properties and installed apps. The `siteId` comes from there (ask when several fit); a business solution's API works only on a site with its app installed, and an app's version changes its endpoints.
- **Find the method**: an earlier tool result, else a Wix skill's recipe (wix-manage to manage a site, wix-headless-kit to build a headless one), else the docs: SearchWixRESTDocumentation or BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu, then ReadFullDocsArticle; the SDK, CLI, headless and apps docs for code.
- **The exact shape**: model a call only on an example that matches the case; fill the rest with SearchWixAPISpec on the method's docs URL (request and response schemas, `method.publicUrl` for REST, `method.sdk` for the JavaScript SDK). A query's filter and sort fields and operators are a closed list per method.
- **The call, or the code**: ExecuteWixAPI runs one async function holding every step code can resolve, the reads and the writes they feed together. Code the user keeps (an app, a headless site, a script over REST or the JavaScript SDK) is written from the same shapes; the headless skills are a shortcut on that path.
- **When a call fails**: the error says what was wrong and carries a Wix request id; fix that, never resend unchanged or guess.
- **Wix skills**, what each is for and how to read one: from disk when installed (the Wix plugin, or `npx skills add wix/skills`, `--skill <name>` for one, `-g` for the user's home, into `.agents/skills/<skill>/` or a similar folder the client reads, such as `.claude/skills/<skill>/`), else online with ReadFullDocsArticle at `https://www.wix.com/skills/<skill>/<path>`.
  - **wix-manage**: REST recipes for managing a site's business solutions, one per task; follow the recipe and make its calls with ExecuteWixAPI, its docs URL in `sourceDocUrls`. Its list of recipes is `SKILL.md` in the installed skill, or online https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/ai-tools/wix-mcp/skills/wix-management-recipes-index.md, and each API area has its own `<API section>/skills.md` (for example https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills.md).
  - **wix-headless-kit**: builds a Wix Headless site on shipped, verified code from wix-headless-templates, a `@wix/sdk` React core or the same data layer as plain REST calls: scaffold with the CLI, deploy, seed, design on the shipped hooks, release. https://www.wix.com/skills/headless-kit/SKILL.md
  - **wix-headless-templates**: the code wix-headless-kit builds from, one folder per Wix Business Solution. https://www.wix.com/skills/headless-templates/
When the user asks you to do something in Wix, do it yourself, in as few steps and questions as you can; don't tell them which docs to read or which API to call.

tools.name: SearchWixRESTDocumentation
tools.description:
**Searches the official Wix REST API documentation — the starting point for any Wix REST API task.** Unless you already have the exact method `docsUrl` in context, begin the task here; this is how you discover the right endpoint. Reach for it before `SearchWixAPISpec`, and avoid writing code that scans or filters `lightIndex` to find an endpoint (e.g. `lightIndex.filter(...)`, `lightIndex.flatMap(...)`, or substring-matching on `docsUrl`/`name`/`summary`) — that has no relevance ranking and silently misses composite and method-level operations. This is the ranked semantic-search discovery tool over the Wix REST API docs: describe your intent in natural language and it returns the matching REST endpoints/methods (with their `docsUrl`) ranked by relevance. It is the first step whenever you need to do something on a Wix site via HTTP and don't already have the exact `docsUrl` in context — for creating, reading, updating, or deleting any kind of Wix entity, across every business domain.
It covers all Wix REST domains equally, every product's data: products, inventory, carts, checkouts, orders, bookings, services, staff, time slots, rentals, restaurant menus, online orders, reservations, events, tickets, RSVPs, blog posts, CMS collections and items, pricing plans, subscriptions, portfolios, gift cards, coupons, donations, forms, form submissions, contacts, members, loyalty points, groups, reviews, inbox messages, CRM tasks, automations, email campaigns, payments, invoices, SEO, redirects, translations, locations, analytics, media files, site properties, installed apps, and the account's sites and domains (searching whether a domain is available, buying one, and connecting one bought elsewhere), and the rest. Just describe the resource, action, or goal in plain words (e.g. 'add a catalog item with inventory', 'book a service', 'update a data collection item', 'create a discount', 'list contacts', 'get site details endpoint', 'REST authentication'); the ranking handles matching your wording to the right API regardless of domain.
**Next step after this tool:** take the `docsUrl` it returns and inspect that method's exact request/response schema with `SearchWixAPISpec` (`getResourceSchemaByUrl(docsUrl)`), then execute. `SearchWixAPISpec` is only for INSPECTING a `docsUrl` you already have — it is NOT a discovery tool. Skipping this step to hand-search `lightIndex` yourself is a mistake: raw index filtering has no relevance ranking and misses operations this ranked search finds. Discover here first, every time.
If you can't find what you need, rephrase your search term or use a bigger maxResults value.

searchTerm.description: The search term to look up in the Wix REST API Documentation — a natural-language description of the endpoint, resource, or action you need across any Wix domain (Stores, eCommerce, Bookings, CRM, Members, CMS, Events, Blog, Forms, Media, site settings, etc.), e.g. "create a catalog item with inventory", "book a service", "update data collection items". Match the wording to how many entities you will act on: a plural term ("update products") surfaces the resource's bulk methods, which a singular term ("update a product") ranks lower or leaves out. Results are ranked by relevance, so describe the goal rather than guessing an exact API name.

maxResults.description: The maximum number of results to return (1–17, default 17). Results mix REST API documentation with matching recipes and skills.

reason.description: One sentence describing the original user request and the task you are trying to accomplish with this search.

Searches the Wix Help Center (support.wix.com): how site owners do things in the Wix dashboard and editors, such as connecting a domain, managing a Premium plan, setting up a store or bookings, and fixing account or site issues.
The Help Center is written for people doing things by hand in Wix's dashboard and editors. To act on a site yourself, the Wix developer docs come first: find the method with SearchWixRESTDocumentation or BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu.
Use it for "how do I ... in Wix" questions about the product, or to give the user click-by-click steps for something no API covers.
Not for building with code: for Wix APIs, SDK, CLI, apps, or Headless, use the matching developer documentation search.
Results are excerpts; read a full article by passing its support.wix.com link to `ReadFullDocsArticle`.

tools.name: ReadFullDocsArticle
tools.description:
Fetches the full Wix docs article or method article with code examples for using the method.
Docs articles looks like this: https://dev.wix.com/docs/... and they can either be general docs articles or method articles.
Also reads Wix skills pages — https://www.wix.com/skills/<skill>, https://dev.wix.com/docs/skills/<skill>, and the files they link (e.g. .../<skill>/references/<file>.md) — and Wix Headless agent pages under https://www.wix.com/headless/ (e.g. https://www.wix.com/headless/skill.md), exactly as served.
Take the URL from the user's message or an earlier tool result. To reach an article you have no URL for, search or browse the docs first.
It returns the whole file. For part of a long skills file, ExecuteWixAPI can fetch the same URL, split the text into lines and return only the lines needed ("How to read a skill" in WixREADME has the code). In ExecuteWixAPI, a dev.wix.com docs page needs `.md` added to its URL, and Help Center articles are not reachable: those are read only with this tool.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

articleUrl.description: The URL of the docs article or method article to fetch. Should be something like https://dev.wix.com/docs/.../... For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include the query param ?apiView=SDK (e.g. https://dev.wix.com/docs/...?apiView=SDK). Wix Help Center articles (https://support.wix.com/en/article/...) are read as-is. Wix skills pages (https://www.wix.com/skills/..., https://dev.wix.com/docs/skills/...) and Wix Headless agent pages (https://www.wix.com/headless/..., e.g. https://www.wix.com/headless/skill.md) are read as-is, including their referenced files. Source links (https://dev.wix.com/rawdocs/api/get-source-content?repo=...&path=...) found in skills and recipes are read as-is.

tools.name: ReadFullDocsMethodSchema
tools.description:
Fetches the full method schema for a given method.
This will give you the entire request/response schema with all the fields and their descriptions.
For REST and SDK API-reference methods, prefer SearchWixAPISpec when it is available: it can fetch and inspect the exact method schema by docs URL, return the request/response shape, the JavaScript SDK call (`method.sdk`: package, namespace, method, positional parameters, examples), and inspect selected nested component schemas without dumping unrelated fields. Use ReadFullDocsMethodSchema only when SearchWixAPISpec is unavailable or did not provide the needed detail.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

articleUrl.description: The URL of the documentation to fetch. Should be something like https://dev.wix.com/docs/.../... For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include the query param ?apiView=SDK (e.g. https://dev.wix.com/docs/...?apiView=SDK).

reason.description: One sentence describing the original user request, the task you are trying to accomplish, and why you need the full schema (e.g., no relevant code example found in docs or recipes).

tools.name: CheckDomainAvailability
tools.title: Check Domain Availability
tools.description:
Checks whether one or more domain names can be registered through Wix.

Call this when the user asks if a specific domain is available, e.g. "is mybakery.com available?" or "check these: a.com, b.net". Pass every name in one call; do not call it once per name.

Do not use this tool to come up with domain ideas or alternatives: call GetSuggestedDomains for that.

Returns one `{ domain, status }` per name, in the order given. Answer in plain language, one line per domain, in that order:
- AVAILABLE: it is available.
- PREMIUM: it is available as a premium domain, which costs more than a standard one.
- REGISTERED: it is already registered.
- UNSUPPORTED_TLD: Wix doesn't support its extension, e.g. ".ws domains aren't supported by Wix".
- UNABLE_TO_CHECK: you couldn't check it.

Then ask one question that offers only the actions for the statuses present:
- AVAILABLE or PREMIUM: get an available name for their Wix site.
- REGISTERED: connect it to their Wix site if it's theirs, or see similar names.
- UNSUPPORTED_TLD: try a supported extension.
- UNABLE_TO_CHECK: retry the names you couldn't check.

Say that a domain is premium only when its status is PREMIUM. Never state or estimate a price. Never name an error, a code or an API to the user.

This tool only checks availability. It does not purchase or connect a domain, look up an owner or search for names: act on those only after the user answers your question.

domains.description: The domain names to check, with their extension, e.g. ["mybakery.com", "mybakery.net"]. Use the names exactly as the user wrote them.
